# Jubilees Chapter 27 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Esau's fury; Rebekah sends Jacob away

---

**27:1** Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing with which his father had blessed him, and he said to himself: "The days of mourning for my father are drawing near; then I will kill my brother Jacob."

**27:2** The words of her older son Esau were reported to Rebekah. She sent for her younger son Jacob and said to him: "Behold, your brother Esau is consoling himself with thoughts of killing you.

**27:3** Now therefore, my son, obey my voice: arise and flee to my brother Laban in Haran.

**27:4** Stay with him for a few days until your brother's fury turns away — until your brother's anger toward you subsides and he forgets what you did to him. Then I will send and bring you back from there. Why should I lose both of you in a single day?"

**27:5** Rebekah went and said to Isaac: "I am weary of my life because of the daughters of Heth. If Jacob takes a wife from the daughters of Heth like these, from the women of the land, what will my life be worth to me?"

**27:6** So Isaac called Jacob, blessed him, and charged him: "You shall not take a wife from the daughters of Canaan.

**27:7** Arise, go to Paddan-aram, to the house of Bethuel your mother's father, and from there take yourself a wife from among the daughters of Laban your mother's brother.

**27:8** May God Almighty bless you and make you fruitful and multiply you, so that you become a company of peoples.

**27:9** And may he give you the blessing of Abraham my father — to you and to your descendants after you — that you may possess the land of your sojournings, which God gave to Abraham."

**27:10** So Isaac sent Jacob away, and he went to Paddan-aram to Laban the son of Bethuel the Aramean, the brother of Rebekah, the mother of Jacob and Esau.

**27:11** When Esau saw that Isaac had blessed Jacob and sent him to Paddan-aram to take a wife from there, and that in blessing him he had charged him saying, "You shall not take a wife from the daughters of Canaan,"

**27:12** And that Jacob had obeyed his father and his mother and gone to Paddan-aram —

**27:13** When Esau saw that the daughters of Canaan displeased his father Isaac,

**27:14** Esau went to Ishmael and took as his wife Mahalath the daughter of Ishmael son of Abraham, the sister of Nebajoth, in addition to the wives he already had.

**27:15** Jacob departed from Beer-sheba and went toward Haran. He came to a certain place and stayed there for the night, because the sun had set. Taking one of the stones of that place, he placed it under his head and lay down there to sleep.

**27:16** He dreamed, and behold, a stairway was set up on the earth with its top reaching to heaven; and behold, the angels of God were ascending and descending on it.

**27:17** And behold, the LORD stood above it and said: "I am the LORD, the God of Abraham your father and the God of Isaac. The land on which you are lying I will give to you and to your descendants.

**27:18** Your descendants will be like the dust of the earth, and you will spread out to the west and to the east and to the north and to the south. And in you and in your descendants all the families of the earth will be blessed.

**27:19** Behold, I am with you and will keep you wherever you go, and will bring you back to this land. For I will not leave you until I have done everything I have promised you."

**27:20** Jacob woke from his sleep and said: "Surely the LORD is in this place, and I did not know it."

**27:21** He was afraid and said: "How awesome is this place! This is none other than the house of God, and this is the gate of heaven."

**27:22** Jacob rose early in the morning and took the stone he had placed under his head and set it up as a standing stone, and he poured oil on top of it.

**27:23** He called the name of that place Bethel, though the city had previously been called Luz.

**27:24** Then Jacob made a vow: "If God will be with me and keep me safe on this journey I am taking, and will give me food to eat and clothing to wear,

**27:25** And if I return safely to my father's house, then the LORD will be my God.

**27:26** And this stone that I have set up as a standing stone will be God's house, and of all that you give me I will give a full tenth to you."

---

*LOGOS notes: Formal rendering following the Ge'ez closely. "Stairway" reflects the Ge'ez/Hebrew sullam without committing to "ladder" (runged) or "stairway" (stepped) — either is defensible. Isaac's second blessing (vv.8-9) expands the Genesis 28:3-4 parallel. The Jubilees account emphasizes the promise-to-Abraham connection more explicitly than MT.*
